trials.name: GRADUATE I
trials.population: Early Alzheimer's disease (mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline to Week 116 in Global Outcome, as Measured by CDR-SB
trials.results_summary: Failed to meet its primary endpoint of slowing clinical decline on the CDR-SB compared to placebo. The trial was formally terminated following the negative readout.

trials.name: GRADUATE II
trials.population: Early Alzheimer's disease (mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline to Week 116 in Global Outcome, as Measured by CDR-SB
trials.results_summary: Failed to meet its primary endpoint of slowing clinical decline on the CDR-SB compared to placebo. The trial was formally terminated alongside the broader development program.

trials.name: SCarlet RoAD
trials.primary_endpoint: Mean Change From Baseline in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SOB) Total Score at Week 104
trials.results_summary: An earlier phase 3 trial that was halted early for futility, failing to show a clinical benefit of gantenerumab in prodromal Alzheimer's disease.

trials.name: Marguerite RoAD
trials.primary_endpoint: Percentage of Participants With Adverse Events (AEs) or Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
trials.results_summary: An earlier phase 3 trial converted into an open-label safety and dosing study after the initial futility analysis of the broader gantenerumab program.

trials.name: DIAN-TU
trials.population: Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer's disease (DIAD) mutation carriers and at-risk family members
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in the DIAN-Multivariate Cognitive Endpoint (DIAN-MCE)
trials.results_summary: The gantenerumab treatment arm and its open-label extension were discontinued based on findings from an interim efficacy analysis and the overall negative status of the drug program.

related_evidence.description: Primary publication of the GRADUATE I and II Phase 3 trials in the New England Journal of Medicine.
Publication detailing the safety and efficacy results from the long-term open-label extension of the DIAN-TU trial involving gantenerumab, confirming the drug's discontinuation.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence base for gantenerumab is highly robust, mature, and definitively negative regarding its clinical efficacy. Across multiple large-scale Phase 3 programs (GRADUATE I, GRADUATE II, SCarlet RoAD, and Marguerite RoAD), gantenerumab consistently failed to meet primary endpoints for slowing clinical and cognitive decline on the CDR-SB in early and prodromal Alzheimer's disease. While the drug showed target engagement by reducing amyloid-beta plaques and shifting downstream tau biomarkers, the magnitude of amyloid clearance was insufficient to translate into a measurable clinical benefit. Following these negative readouts, Hoffmann-La Roche terminated the GRADUATE program, and the drug's open-label arm in the DIAN-TU platform trial was also discontinued.
discrepancies: The document states an enrollment 'n' of 1,965 participants for the two trials, but the ClinicalTrials.gov registries record a combined enrollment of 2,028 (1,053 in NCT03444870 and 975 in NCT03443973). This discrepancy often arises between the number of enrolled/consented participants (registry) versus those finally randomized or analyzed (paper).
The document does not explicitly note that the GRADUATE trials were formally 'Terminated' by the sponsor, a status reflected in the registry following the program's overall discontinuation.
